text:
maria: Ran a 24h perf profile on continuous batching + prefix KV cache. Surprising regression in cache hit-rate when batch composition mixes a lot of unique prefixes. dumping numbers + a quick proposal for discussion.

tom: can you paste the actual numbers and impact on p99 / token cost?

maria: TL;DR: continuous batching + default FIFO queue gave ~9% throughput uplift and ~2.3% model-time improvement on avg latency, BUT global prefix hit-rate dropped from ~42% -> ~33% on our test workload. That hit-rate loss maps to ~+5.6% net token cost and small p95 regressions for short prompts (<=64 tokens).

maria: profiler notes:
- 72% of processing batches had >1 unique prefix key (high heterogeneity).
- When batches mix hot and cold prefixes, later items in the batch miss because KV slots haven't been populated/warmed. continuous batching increases interleaving.
- Observed warmup window: first request that writes prefix -> subsequent reuse happens only if next requests hit same slot within ~10-20ms on same instance. continuous batching reduces that locality.

maria: sample grouping helper we used in the analysis (pseudo-Python):
```python
def normalize_prompt(p):
    # strip deterministic metadata, trim, collapse whitespace
    p = re.sub(r"\bTS=\\d+\b", "", p)
    p = re.sub(r"\bSID=[A-Za-z0-9\-]+\b", "", p)
    return ' '.join(p.split())[:1024]

def prefix_bucket_key(prompt, k=128, buckets=256):
    h = sha256(normalize_prompt(prompt).encode('utf-8')).digest()
    return int.from_bytes(h[:4], 'big') % buckets

# group requests by prefix_bucket_key before forming micro-batches
```

kevin: that aligns with what i suspected — batch mixing cold/hot prefixes kills cache locality. did you try a grouping-by-key policy in the scheduler?

maria: yes. experiments:
- grouping by prefix_bucket (wait up to 8ms to form same-bucket micro-batch) recovered most of the hit-rate (back to ~39%) but increased avg latency for latency-sensitive single-turn calls by ~6-9ms p50.
- prefetching top-K prefixes per model instance (seed during idle cycles) recovered hit-rate with <2ms additional latency in microbench.
- naive prefix-normalization (over-aggressive) caused a small correctness risk when we stripped useful context; we constrained normalization to deterministic metadata only.

lisa: could we do hybrid: try same-bucket grouping for up to X ms, fall back to FIFO when latency budget would be exceeded? seems like a practical latency vs hit-rate tradeoff.

maria: exactly my proposal: hybrid policy:
1) if request has x-latency-sensitive header (client hint), route to FIFO path (no extra wait).
2) otherwise try micro-batch grouping by prefix_bucket with a small max-wait (8ms) and a min-batch-size of 2.
3) background prefetcher seeds top-100 prefixes per model/region when GPU idle.

tom: how risky is prefix-normalized keying for semantic correctness? like merging prompts that differ only in user-visible whitespace or small tokens.

maria: we will not do semantic normalization. normalization only strips deterministic metadata (timestamps, session ids) via regex whitelist/blacklist and collapses contiguous whitespace. Also add an opt-out header per request (x-kv-cache=off) for customers who want strict behavior. we'll run synthetic QA tests.

ci-bot: perf/regression-checker: branch "batch-prefix-hotfix" lowered cache-hit by 8% on canary. logs: http://ci.internal/reports/1234 (see diff graphs) :warning:

kevin: can we gate the new batching policy to dedicated pools first? Also expose per-route per-model prefix-hit-rate so product teams can opt-in if their workload benefits.

maria: plan:
- implement prefix-bucket grouping behind a feature flag scoped to pool type (dedicated first)
- add prefetch service that seeds top-K prefixes per model instance (configurable)
- instrument per-route/model prefix-hit-rate + token-cost delta and add to console dashboards
- run a 1-week A/B with 5% traffic for initial measurement

lisa: +1. i'll build a test harness that simulates mixed chat (short prompts) and batch (long prompts) traffic so we can quantify p50/p95/p99 and hit-rate tradeoffs.

maria: thanks — i'll open the PR with tests + CI job and tag you all for review. :rocket:
